item.title: Character Creation
item.description:
To help you create a character that is Stockholm D&D Legal, we have included a step-by-step process both for those who use D&DBeyond and those who do not. If you are familiar with D&D 5.5e, you can simply read the summary.

If you are new to D&D, we strongly recommend that you choose a character without spellcasting, i.e. Barbarian or Fighter.

A summary of our character creation rules

  • Start at level 3.
  • Any official D&D-source from the approved list.
  • Any of the allowed classes and species.
  • Point buy or Standard array. (Rolling for stats is not permitted.)
  • Fixed hit-points.
  • No alignment
  • Starting equipment, one common magic item from the magic items list, + 100gp.
  • Feats and Multi-classing are allowed.
  • You may come from any D&D-esque world, including homebrew; we are setting agnostic.
  • Follow the spirit of the game, have fun together, don’t cheat or try to find loopholes.
  • You are responsible for your character, be mindful of the whole table.

Using D&D Beyond character creator:

  1. Sources: We support officially published materials (i.e. Player’s Handbook etc.), you can find a full list further down in the document, we do not allow any Unearthed Arcana.
  2. On D&D Beyond, this means deselecting any sources other than Core Rules and Expanded Rules.
  3. Optional Features are permitted.
  4. For Advancement we use Milestone-levelling
  5. Use Fixed hit point type
  6. We use prerequisites for Feats and Multiclass requirements
  7. Character privacy: Public
  8. Choose a Class
  9. Set your level to 3
    Note that multiclassing is allowed.
  10. Select Proficiencies and Class Features
  11. Choose a Background.
    Note that Custom Background isn’t currently supported¹ in 5.5e.
  12. Set your Ability Score Increases
  13. Choose a Species
  14. Select Proficiencies and Species Features
    Ability scores generation method: Point Buy or Standard Array. 1. (Rolling for stats is not permitted.)
    Choose Starting Equipment (you may sell these items at half 1. price)
  15. Under Currency add 100 gold
  16. Choose a common magic item from the list below.
  17. Add appearance, backstory, and other character details.
    Note that we do not use alignment or lifestyle.

¹ In 5.5e it is an optional rule and D&D Beyond doesn’t currently support the 5.5e version. When they do we may permit it.

item.title: Registering your character
item.description: We use a discord bot to manage participation at the tables at our events. This means that you must register your character with the bot @D&Dtabler from our discord server in order to join a table. To do so, first make sure you have either a shareable link to your character on D&D Beyond or a PDF or images of your character sheet handy. Then send a direct message to the @D&Dtabler bot with the command &newcharacter. The bot will then ask you to supply the relevant information and you can confirm that everything is correct at the end.

item.title: Playing your first game
item.description:
Playing your first game

Make sure your character is Guild-legal, if you are unsure about it feel free to share the character or any questions in the channel #beginner-help. Before you go on your first adventure, your character may sell any unwanted items from their starting equipment for half the listed price (PHB), and may buy any item listed in the PHB or further down in this document.
You can purchase any item found in the PHB for the listed price, as well as items found in this document under the “Shopping”-section.
You should know who your character is, being able to describe what they look like is nice, but you are responsible for knowing the mechanics of your character: Know what your species and class features, as well as spells and other abilities, do before the game starts. Nobody wants to look at the rules mid-game.

item.title: Bot Commands
item.description:
All commands are prefixed with &. Required parameters are shown in <angle brackets> and optional parameters in [square brackets].

General

&botinfo

&botinfo

Display the bot version.

&companions

&companions [edition] [layout]

Render a graph of characters who’ve adventured with characters by edition.

The layout controls what the graph will look like, choose one of the available options if you want a different style.

item.title: Sensitive subjects and discomfort
item.description:
Sensitive Subjects and Discomfort

Games may involve subjects or depictions that make a player uncomfortable, or other people at the table may speak or behave in a way that makes a player uncomfortable. If there are any subjects that may be triggering for you, making the Dungeon Master aware of these beforehand is helpful. Most Dungeon Masters will check if there are any sensitive subjects that should be avoided beforehand. They may also present one or more Safety Tools with which a player can signal discomfort so they can steer away from a sensitive subject or stop an insensitive behaviour.
A list of various safety tools have been compiled in this document: Safety Tools.

item.title: Rewards
item.description:
Every adventure you play in Stockholm D&D is worth half a level, as long as your character survives the adventure.

You start at level 3. After surviving 2 adventures (0.5 levels each) you will be level 4.

After each adventure, the Dungeon Master decides how much gold the party gets, based on the tier played:

Tier Level played Standard gold Maximum gold
1 3-4 100 150
2 5-6 150 225
3 7-8 230 345
4 9-10 340 510
5 11-12 510 765
6 13-14 760 1140
7 15-16 1140 1710
8 17-18 1710 2565
9 19-20 2560 3840

Acquiring loot on adventures

You may acquire permanent and consumable magic items in your adventures. Permanent magic items acquired in a session can never be carried out of that session. Consumable magic items can, but this must be explicitly stated by the Dungeon Master, who should specify what the item is and how many times it can be used before it is consumed.

item.title: Before each adventure
item.description:
Before each adventure

The expectation is that you come to the table with your entire character sheet sorted:

  • What items you are bringing, limited by carrying capacity.
  • You have done your downtime and shopping prior to sitting down at the table.
  • Do remember to register the downtime activity with the bot.
  • You know how your class & racial features work.
  • Spells are chosen and you know how they work.
  • Ask in #beginner-help before the session if you are unsure about anything. Note: You can only do one downtime-activity before an adventure. Unused downtime is lost.

Items that recharge at dawn

We can assume that sufficient downtime between adventures have passed to fully recharge any rechargeable items. At the start of each session you start with all charges available unless the Dungeon Master decrees otherwise.

item.title: Downtime
item.description:
Downtime

After your character has survived an adventure, you may perform one downtime activity, these are: Crafting, Learning a new language or tool, Spell scribing, and Buying life insurance.
There is no set time for how long downtime is but it cannot be used for repeated casting of spells, or similar activities, to create permanent effects that may or may not impact game mechanics. To avoid complications downtime activities are limited to the ones described in this document.
To log your downtime, use the &character command after your Dungeon Master has logged the adventure you went on.
Note: This must be done before your next adventure starts. Downtime does not stack.

item.title: If you are unhappy with your character
item.description: Before your character reaches level 5, you may change a few things — subspecies, subclass, class features, background, feats, ability score increases, chosen spells, and descriptive details.

item.title: General clarifications
item.description:
General Clarifications

We understand that some rules and rules interactions can be confusing, we ask that you first look to the Sage Advice-compendium, where you will find the official rulings for D&D 5e and 5.5e: https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/sae

Do we follow Rules-As-Written (RAW)?

Yes, in general, there are two exceptions: Alignment and Lifestyle expenses. We follow everything else that is official in the rulebooks.
Note: Each DM has their own style and can apply any house-rules they want.

Safety Tools
item.description:
How to use this page

While it isn’t a requirement for our Dungeon Masters to use Safety Tools it is strongly recommended. This document is a collection of tools to pick and choose from for a Dungeon Master. It is also a reference for players and budding Dungeon Masters.

The tools are grouped by pre-session tools that are ideally used before the game starts to set expectations, in-session tools to handle issues that occur in-game, and post-session tools to follow up on events after a session.
